references.text: God promises to send his angel ahead of the people to lead them to the promised land, the same promise given here after the golden calf sin.
God repeats the promise to send an angel ahead of the Israelites to drive out the Canaanites.
God visits the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, reflecting the warning that he will visit their sin.
The fulfillment of God's judgment on the people who sinned, where they die in the wilderness as punishment.
Vengeance and recompense belong to the Lord; he will visit at his appointed time.
The Lord will visit and punish on the set day, the same theme of delayed judgment.
God will raise up shepherds to lead the people, parallel to the angel who leads Israel.
Paul speaks of the day of wrath when God's righteous judgment will be revealed, corresponding to the day of visitation.
The author refers to those who sinned in the wilderness and experienced God's judgment, including the golden calf incident.
Malachi alludes directly to the Exodus motif but turns it from a warning about God's absence into a promise of his presence.
Both verses confirm the theological principle that God's grace does not cancel the consequences of sin.
A direct continuation in the same event showing the tension between God's judgment and Moses' prayer for his presence.
Creates a theological contrast between immediate judgment on sin and final restoration.
